question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $W,$ and the vector $b$ above. If the normal equation for the corresponding weighted least-squares problem $W\,Ax=Wb$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}a & 7 \\ 7 & b\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ c\end{aligned}]
$$

what is the value of $a+b+c?$
question.worked_solution:
To get the normal equation corresponding to $W\,Ax=Wb,$ we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by $(W\,A)^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(W\,A)^{T}\cdot W\,Ax & =(W\,A)^{T}\cdot Wb \\ {A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)Ax & ={A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)b\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since

$$
{W}^{T}W=[\begin{aligned}{1}^{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & {3}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {2}^{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 9 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}],
$$

our normal equation can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 9 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 9 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 9 & 9 \\ 4 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ -9 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}14 & 7 \\ 7 & 17\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -11\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=14+17+(-11)=20.
$$
